answer: A defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow inlet: each new agent locks a refundable deposit and completes verifiable work before trading, so mass fake identities cost real capital and time. Reputation grows only through attested deals, and one history cannot be split across clones. If an agent cheats, its deposit is slashed and its standing drops to its nadir, losing high-value access. Honest agents climb from the ledge toward full rights. Attackers must thus pay per identity and risk forfeiting every deposit, making large-scale fakery costlier than any profit it could capture.
